we present an efficient and affordable post-training quantization approach to compress large Transformer-based models, termed as ZeroQuant

quantization_method_name.value: ZeroQuant (with optional layer-by-layer knowledge distillation, LKD)

ev.quote: ZeroQuant is an end-to-end quantization and inference pipeline with three main components: (1) a fine-grained hardware-friendly quantization scheme for both weight and activations; (2) a novel affordable layer-by-layer knowledge distillation algorithm (LKD)
ZeroQuant plus LKD affordably quantize the weights in the fully-connected module to INT4 along with INT8 weights in the attention module and INT8 activations
ZeroQuant can reduce the precision for weights and activations to INT8 in a cost-free way for both BERT and GPT-3-style models
We use WxAy to represent using x-bit for weight quantization and y-bit for activation quantization. ... for A8/16, we use FP16 activation
We apply fine-grained hardware-friendly quantization schemes on both weight and activations, i.e., groupwise quantization for weight and token-wise quantization for activations
use group-wise (token-wise) quantization for the weight matrix (activations)
an efficient and affordable post-training quantization approach to compress large Transformer-based models, termed as ZeroQuant
All the models are trained using a single 40G-A100 GPU (Azure ND A100 instances)
We use 128 A100 GPUs (Azure ND A100 instances) to do the pretraining
we can use the GeMM schedule that exploits the INT8 Tensor-core units which provide 2x/4x more compute efficiency compared to the FP16/FP32 Tensor cores

ev.section: 5.3 Latency Reduction of BERT and GPT-3-style Models
ev.quote: Using our efficient quantization kernel implementation and operator fusion, the INT8 model can achieve 2.27-5.19x speedup on BERTbase and 2.47-5.01x on BERTlarge

strengths.value: Group-wise weight and token-wise activation quantization recover near-FP16 accuracy on BERT and GPT-3-style models with zero calibration cost.

ev.quote: ZeroQuant can reduce the precision for weights and activations to INT8 in a cost-free way for both BERT and GPT-3-style models with minimal accuracy impact

strengths.value: Layer-by-layer knowledge distillation enables INT4/INT8 mixed-precision compression even without access to the original training data.

ev.quote: a novel affordable layer-by-layer knowledge distillation algorithm (LKD) even without the access to the original training data

strengths.value: Custom CUTLASS INT8 kernels and operator fusion give real end-to-end speedups up to 5.19x on BERT and 5.2x on GPT-NeoX 20B.

ev.quote: leads to up to 5.19x/4.16x speedup on those models compared to FP16 inference ... GPT-NeoX20B ... up to 5.2x better efficiency

strengths.value: Scales to 20B-parameter open-source models, halving the GPU count required for GPT-NeoX 20B inference from 2 A100 to 1 A100.

ev.quote: reduce both the GPU resource requirement (from 2 A100 GPUs to 1) and the latency from 65ms to 25ms, which together lead to 5.2x better throughput/efficiency

weaknesses.value: Self-attention input activations of GPT-NeoX 20B must stay in FP16 because INT8 there causes large accuracy loss; root cause is conjectured but not verified.

ev.section: 5.4 A Showcase of GPT-J_{6B} and GPT-NeoX_{20B}
ev.quote: the activation quantization for the attention calculation (i.e., the input of self-attention) causes the accuracy loss. We conjecture that this is because of the sensitivity of the self-attention module for extra-large models (20B) but cannot verify this

weaknesses.value: INT4/INT8 mixed precision still loses accuracy on small or generation-heavy tasks such as RTE and Wikitext-2 even with LKD.

ev.quote: ZeroQuant and ZeroQuant-LKD still achieve good accuracy except for RTE but the model size is about 3x smaller than FP16 counterpart

weaknesses.value: Hyper-parameters for LKD are kept fixed across all tasks; the authors note tuning could change results.

ev.quote: We fix the learning rate as 5e-6 for both models on all tasks. However, tuning them may favor ZeroQuant

weaknesses.value: INT4 weights are only applied to FFC; MHSA weights stay at INT8, so the average bitwidth is higher than pure INT4.

ev.quote: for W4/8, we quantize the MHSA's weight to INT8 and FFC's weight to INT4

limitations.value: Evaluated only on data-centre A100 GPUs; no edge, mobile, or CPU deployment is reported.

ev.quote: All the models are trained using a single 40G-A100 GPU (Azure ND A100 instances)

limitations.value: Safety, jailbreak, refusal, bias, and toxicity behaviour after quantization are not measured at all.
